newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CRICKET-TEAM SPIRIT KEY TO ASHES SUCCESS SAYS TAYLOR.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-TEAM SPIRIT KEY TO ASHES SUCCESS SAYS TAYLOR.

text.p: Team spirit will be the key to a successful Ashes tour of England predicted Australia's captain Mark Taylor after their seven-match limited overs series against South Africa ended on Sunday.
Yet despite Australia winning the test rubber 2-1 and the one-dayers 4-3, question marks still hang over Taylor's own place in the touring squad which is due to be announced on Thursday.
"The team spirit is something we've got to take to England," said Taylor.
"All the away tours I have been on have generally succeeded when we have a good team spirit going. You are away for a long time and you need to keep the spirit going in the side.
"If we can keep that for four months in England we will be hard to beat."
Australia won 14 and lost only four matches of their 18-game tour of South Africa, but Taylor's role as captain has come increasingly into question as his batting form has utterly deserted him.
He has not scored a test 50 since the end of 1995 and in his two one-day appearances against South Africa he was embarrassingly out of touch, making just 17 agonising runs from 68 balls.
He handed over the captaincy for the final five one-day internationals to Ian Healy.
"I decided to rest my back but I was available to play if I was needed," said Taylor. "There was never a point where Ian Healy and (coach) Geoff Marsh said I couldn't play.
"We'll have to wait and see what the selectors do."

The emergence of Jason Gillespie as a bowling foil for Glenn McGrath was picked out as the main plus of the tour by Taylor, who also foresaw a successful tour of England after series wins over West Indies and South Africa.
"Our chances are very good in England but having said that it's 0-0 at the moment.
"The thing we have to do there is what we did against the West Indies and here against South Africa and start well.
"I should imagine we'll be firm favourites as we've won there the last two times and have been playing well over the last year or so but that's when it gets dangerous.
"The Poms have very little pressure on them and have had a couple of good wins against New Zealand so we shouldn't underestimate them."
South African skipper Hansie Cronje said the series defeats had taught his side a few lessons.
"We made a selection error or two and maybe relied too much on younger guys rather than putting older players up the top of the order," he said.
"We didn't have players like Gary Kirsten and Andrew Hudson -- we shouldn't panic and make change for the sake of change. We should maybe pick a squad of 14 and stick with them for six months.
"It wasn't fair to rate us as the number one test playing country -- I think the system was probably wrong -- and we never thought of ourselves as that.
"But the ultimate now will be to beat Australia in Australia next year and that's what we are going to start working towards now."
